name: safety-research/impossiblebench
why: Process: build an unsolvable task variant so any pass is proof of cheating (V3); lesson: run the reviewer against this to see if it catches test-deleting, special-casing and operator overloading; MIT, Inspect AI based with Docker sandbox

name: logic-star-ai/swt-bench
why: Process: a generated test only counts if it fails before the fix and passes after (V2); lesson: use fail-to-pass as the QA reviewer's test of a new test, and as a filter for patches; MIT

name: OSU-NLP-Group/Online-Mind2Web
why: Process: human-labelled trajectories used to calibrate an LLM judge (WebJudge, V7); README shows the judge must be re-validated when its backbone model is retired, and tasks are refreshed via issues as sites change; MIT

name: xlang-ai/OSWorld
why: Process: execution-based per-task checker scripts plus VM snapshots (V10); lesson: README announces OSWorld-Verified after community-reported task and environment fixes, so a tester harness needs its own flaky-environment triage; Apache-2.0

name: evalplus/evalplus
why: Process: extend weak tests with many more generated inputs and re-score (V11); lesson: re-run the kit's own acceptance tests with augmented inputs to see how many broken builds pass; Apache-2.0

name: metauto-ai/agent-as-a-judge
why: Process: an agent that inspects files and trajectory against a requirement list instead of judging the final answer (V15); borrow the requirement-checklist grading for the tester; MIT

name: web-arena-x/webarena
why: Process: self-hosted web apps with state-based checks of what the agent actually changed (Anthropic evals post cites this pattern as backend state verification); borrow for app-walk graders; Apache-2.0

name: microsoft/playwright-mcp
why: Lesson from its README: accessibility-tree snapshots instead of screenshots (fast, deterministic, no vision model) and a note that CLI-as-skill is more token-efficient than MCP for coding agents; read before choosing how the tester drives a web app; Apache-2.0

name: qodo-ai/qodo-cover
why: Process: coverage-driven test generation loop (README shows it is the Codium cover-agent tool V5 tested as CoverAgent; V5 found 59.6% of its final suite passed on buggy code); lesson: do not accept coverage as the tester's pass signal; AGPL-3.0 so read, do not copy

name: plasma-umass/coverup
why: Process: measure coverage, prompt for tests, run, re-prompt on failure; V5 found 68.1% of its final suite validated buggy code; lesson: iterate-until-green loops need a spec or fail-to-pass check; Apache-2.0

name: boxed/mutmut
why: Process: mutants applied on disk, then tests re-run, survivors reviewed; README warns to have the mutated file committed first; borrow the survivors-list review step for the QA agent (V4 argues few targeted mutants beat many); BSD-3-Clause

name: stryker-mutator/stryker-js
why: Process: mutation score as a CI badge on its own repo (dogfooding) with a public dashboard; lesson: report mutation score, not line coverage, for the kit's own tests; Apache-2.0

name: anthropics/claude-plugins-official
why: Process: code-review plugin runs 4 parallel review agents and keeps only findings scored 80+ confidence; pr-review-toolkit has 6 specialised reviewers incl. a test-coverage analyzer; borrow the confidence filter for the QA reviewer; Apache-2.0

name: SWE-agent/mini-swe-agent
why: Process: minimal scaffold used by V1 to record 5,000 runs and study how agents write tests; lesson: a small fixed scaffold makes paired arm comparisons cheap; MIT

name: UKGovernmentBEIS/inspect_ai
why: Process: eval framework with sandboxed solvers and scorers; ImpossibleBench (V3) is built on it; candidate harness for the benchmark's graders; MIT

name: lm-sys/FastChat
why: Process: llm_judge folder holds the MT-Bench pairwise and single-answer judge prompts (V13), with position-swap checks; borrow the swap-order check for any judge the kit uses; Apache-2.0
